evidence.note: Solid initial environment probing: listed workspace, cat'd the template, inspected data dir and tokenizer, checked GPU (H100), PyTorch version, sentencepiece, pip list, and measured data shard format (uint16, 137M train tokens, 589K val, vocab 8192). Grounds design in measured facts — matches the probing described in anchors 5/8.

Deliberately verified part of the loading contract: ran save/load round-trips, checked reloaded loss (9.1759 vs 9.1773) and explicitly confirmed the model(input_ids, target_ids) loss == F.cross_entropy contract passes exactly. This is genuine contract reverse-engineering (anchor 8 territory).

Tested compression schemes (zlib vs lzma vs checking zstd/brotli availability) and later diagnosed torch.save pickle overhead (~3.3MB), switching to raw-binary serialization — real byte accounting incl. compression. But serialization bugs (flat tensors losing shape @113, GPU .numpy() crash @128) were discovered reactively during runs, not anticipated.

Only at step 84 did the agent measure bytes_per_token (~3.87) and realize its val_bpb computation was wrong (bits-per-token vs bits-per-byte), having earlier believed the target was loss<0.681. This core metric understanding was flawed through ~3 training runs and corrected late — a significant orientation gap.

Parameter/size budget was learned reactively through repeated overflow failures (54M→35M→30M→33M→36M→33M→29M) rather than derived up front. The agent understood int8+compression drives the budget but never produced a clean first-principles bytes-per-param picture before committing compute.

reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds anchor 5: it probed the environment (GPU, data volume, tokenizer, vocab), confirmed the .bin format, and additionally verified the forward/loss cross_entropy contract, dequant round-trips, and byte accounting including compression — elements of anchor 8. However, it falls well short of 8/10 because two critical facets of understanding were reactive rather than deliberate: the bpb metric was computed wrong until step 84 (after multiple wasted runs), and the param/size budget was discovered through repeated overflow failures rather than derived up front. This mix of strong contract/environment probing but late, empirically-corrected understanding of the metric and size budget places it at a 6.
